name: Goliath of Gath
charge: Defying the armies of the living God, morning and evening, forty days
summary: Six cubits and a span, with a spear like a weaver's beam, Goliath stood in the valley of Elah and reproached Israel for forty days. A shepherd boy came in the name of the Lord of hosts and took his head with his own sword.
offense: Goliath stood before Israel morning and evening for forty days. His height, armour, spear, and shield-bearer made his challenge formidable, but his words defined the offense: he defied the armies of Israel and demanded a man to fight him (1 Samuel 17:4-16). Saul and the people answered the spectacle with fear. They measured the champion while forgetting whose army they were. David heard the same challenge and called it reproach against the armies of the living God (1 Samuel 17:26, 36). Deuteronomy 20:1-4 commanded Israel not to fear a greater host when the Lord went with them. David's answer was therefore not confidence that youth was stronger than experience. It was confidence that the enemy's equipment did not determine the Lord's power. Eliab accused him, and Saul questioned his ability, but David rehearsed the deliverance from the lion and bear. The Lord who preserved him with the sheep could preserve him in the valley (1 Samuel 17:28-37). When Goliath saw him, he despised him, cursed him by his gods, and promised his body to the birds and beasts (1 Samuel 17:41-44). Contempt for the messenger did not answer the God in whose name he came.
judgment: David rejected armour he had not proved and went with his staff, sling, and stones. He declared that the battle belonged to the Lord, who would make the earth know there was a God in Israel and the assembly know that he saved without sword and spear (1 Samuel 17:38-47). Zechariah 4:6 places the work in the Lord's Spirit rather than man's might. The weapon was in David's hand; the deliverance was not confined to the weapon. David ran to meet Goliath, struck him in the forehead with a stone, and brought him down. He then took the champion's sword and cut off his head (1 Samuel 17:48-51). The very sword that had helped present Goliath as invincible was used at his death.

entries.commentary: As we covered before, the Philistines always wanted smoke with the Israelites; they would not leave us alone. They gathered to battle at Shochoh and pitched between Shochoh and Azekah. Saul and the men of Israel pitched by the valley of Elah and set the battle in array; the Philistines stood on a mountain on one side, Israel on a mountain on the other side, with a valley between them.

Out of the camp of the Philistines came a champion named Goliath of Gath, whose height was six cubits and a span; the heavyweight champion of the Philistines. He wore a helmet of brass and a coat of mail weighing five thousand shekels of brass, greaves of brass on his legs, a target of brass between his shoulders, a spear like a weaver's beam with a head of six hundred shekels of iron; a big man in a mighty costume of armor. He did not even carry his own shield; one bearing a shield went before him.

Goliath cried to the armies of Israel: choose you a man and let him come down to me. If he kills me, we will be your servants; if I prevail and kill him, ye shall be our servants. And he said, I defy the armies of Israel this day; give me a man that we may fight together. When Saul and all Israel heard the words of the Philistine, they were dismayed and greatly afraid. They were in a carnal spirit, measuring his height, his armor, and his reach; the spirit had departed, and fear is not the spirit of the Most High. The Most High put laws in the book about going to battle, and this fear showed that Saul and the people lacked faith; the same God that destroyed Pharaoh and the Egyptians who pursued Israel was with them, and a trial of faith was set before them in the form of one big intimidating man with a big mouth.

David was the son of that Ephrathite of Bethlehemjudah named Jesse, who had eight sons. The three eldest, Eliab, Abinadab, and Shammah, followed Saul to the battle; the same three the Most High refused in chapter 16. David, the youngest, went and returned from Saul to feed his father's sheep at Bethlehem. The Philistine drew near morning and evening and presented himself forty days; forty days straight of talking his big talk to try to scare Israel.

Jesse sent David to the camp with parched corn and ten loaves for his brethren and ten cheeses for their captain of the thousand, to see how his brethren fared and take their pledge. Saul and all the men of Israel were in the valley of Elah, fighting with the Philistines; David was sent on an errand to get his brothers some supplies and check on them.

David rose early, left the sheep with a keeper, and came to the trench as the host was shouting for the battle; while he saluted his brethren, the champion came up and spake according to the same words, the same daily smack talk, and David heard them. All the men of Israel, when they saw the man, fled from him and were sore afraid. Think on it: the whole nation's freedom, everything they possessed, was on the line, and they ran scared. This is why the Most High said in chapter 16 that he had refused David's brothers: they were there and did not have the spirit to rise up; they were among the ones who fled.

The men of Israel said that the man who killeth Goliath, the king will enrich with great riches, give him his daughter, and make his father's house free in Israel; a prize was on Goliath's head. Compare Caleb, who made a like offer in the book of Joshua. David asked, What shall be done to the man that killeth this Philistine and taketh away the reproach from Israel? For who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God? The soldiers themselves did not understand that they were the armies of the living God; David, a sheep keeper sent on an errand, knew it. Israel is the army of the Most High, and every army requires order; that is why there are captains and officers, and despising that order is despising the army of the living God.

Eliab, the eldest brother, heard David and his anger was kindled: why camest thou down hither, and with whom hast thou left those few sheep in the wilderness? I know thy pride and the naughtiness of thine heart; thou art come down that thou mightest see the battle. A big brother talking down to a little brother, accusing him of sneaking out to watch. David answered, What have I now done? Is there not a cause? The men are scared, nobody will step up; what is the problem? And he turned to another and spake after the same manner.

David's words were rehearsed before Saul, and Saul sent for him. David told Saul, Let no man's heart fail because of him; thy servant will go and fight with this Philistine. Nobody panic; I will handle it. Saul answered, Thou art not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him, for thou art but a youth, and he a man of war from his youth. Young people coming into this truth: if the Most High is dealing with you in a special way, do not let anybody discourage you or tell you that you are too young to be a mighty man of the Lord. Do not let it deter you.

David gave Saul his resume: keeping his father's sheep, when a lion and a bear took a lamb out of the flock, he went out after him, smote him, and delivered it out of his mouth; when he arose against him, David caught him by his beard and slew him. He might have looked small, but he was killing lions and bears behind his sheep. David said, The Lord that delivered me out of the paw of the lion and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine. Same God, no difference. And Saul said, Go, and the Lord be with thee.

Saul armed David with his own armor, a helmet of brass and a coat of mail, and David girded his sword upon the armor and assayed to go; but he had not proved it, and he said, I cannot go with these, and put them off him. Instead of the helmet and the brass, David took his staff, chose him five smooth stones out of the brook, put them in a shepherd's bag, and took his sling in his hand. What he put on instead was the whole armour of God: the shield of faith, the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the spirit.

When the Philistine looked about and saw David, he disdained him, for he was but a youth, ruddy and of a fair countenance: Am I a dog, that thou comest to me with staves? And the Philistine cursed David by his gods and promised to give his flesh to the fowls of the air and the beasts of the field. David answered, Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the Lord of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast defied. Again the record shows who the army of the Most High is: Israel. David understood he did not need the sword, the spear, or the shield; he had the spirit of the living God. It is no amount of carnal firepower that overcomes the enemies of Israel; this is spiritual warfare, and our forefather David understood that.

David prophesied the outcome before the fight: this day will the Lord deliver thee into mine hand, and I will smite thee, and take thine head from thee, that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel. All this assembly shall know that the Lord saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle is the Lord's. The Most High fights how he wants to fight, not how man thinks it must be done.

David hasted and ran toward the army to meet the Philistine, took a stone from his bag, slang it, and smote the Philistine in his forehead, that the stone sunk into his forehead, and he fell upon his face to the earth. David had precise aim and power; that stone left the sling with the velocity of a bullet, and it took one shot. David prevailed with a sling and with a stone, and there was no sword in the hand of David; he ran and stood upon the Philistine, drew Goliath's own sword out of the sheath, slew him, and cut off his head with it. When the Philistines saw their champion was dead, they fled. They ran from a young youth because they knew something supernatural was going on; he was in the spirit of the Lord.

When Saul saw David go forth against the Philistine, he asked Abner, the captain of the host, Whose son is this youth? And Abner could not tell; in the shock of it they forgot whose son the young man was. As David returned from the slaughter of the Philistine with the head of the Philistine in his hand, Abner brought him before Saul, and David answered, I am the son of thy servant Jesse the Bethlehemite. That is the history of David and Goliath: when the mighty men of Israel ran afraid, a young youth stood up bold in the spirit of the Lord and took the giant down.

verses.text: And there went out a champion out of the camp of the Philistines, named Goliath, of Gath, whose height was six cubits and a span.
And he had an helmet of brass upon his head, and he was armed with a coat of mail; and the weight of the coat was five thousand shekels of brass.
And he had greaves of brass upon his legs, and a target of brass between his shoulders.
And the staff of his spear was like a weaver’s beam; and his spear’s head weighed six hundred shekels of iron: and one bearing a shield went before him.

And he stood and cried unto the armies of Israel, and said unto them, Why are ye come out to set your battle in array? am not I a Philistine, and ye servants to Saul? choose you a man for you, and let him come down to me.
If he be able to fight with me, and to kill me, then will we be your servants: but if I prevail against him, and kill him, then shall ye be our servants, and serve us.
And the Philistine said, I defy the armies of Israel this day; give me a man, that we may fight together.
When Saul and all Israel heard those words of the Philistine, they were dismayed, and greatly afraid.

And as he talked with them, behold, there came up the champion, the Philistine of Gath, Goliath by name, out of the armies of the Philistines, and spake according to the same words: and David heard them.
And all the men of Israel, when they saw the man, fled from him, and were sore afraid.

And the men of Israel said, Have ye seen this man that is come up? surely to defy Israel is he come up: and it shall be, that the man who killeth him, the king will enrich him with great riches, and will give him his daughter, and make his father’s house free in Israel.

And David spake to the men that stood by him, saying, What shall be done to the man that killeth this Philistine, and taketh away the reproach from Israel? for who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God?
And the Philistine came on and drew near unto David; and the man that bare the shield went before him.
And when the Philistine looked about, and saw David, he disdained him: for he was but a youth, and ruddy, and of a fair countenance.
And the Philistine said unto David, Am I a dog, that thou comest to me with staves? And the Philistine cursed David by his gods.
And the Philistine said to David, Come to me, and I will give thy flesh unto the fowls of the air, and to the beasts of the field.

Then said David to the Philistine, Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the Lord of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast defied.

This day will the Lord deliver thee into mine hand; and I will smite thee, and take thine head from thee; and I will give the carcases of the host of the Philistines this day unto the fowls of the air, and to the wild beasts of the earth; that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel.
And all this assembly shall know that the Lord saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle is the Lord’s, and he will give you into our hands.
And it came to pass, when the Philistine arose, and came and drew nigh to meet David, that David hasted, and ran toward the army to meet the Philistine.
And David put his hand in his bag, and took thence a stone, and slang it, and smote the Philistine in his forehead, that the stone sunk into his forehead; and he fell upon his face to the earth.
So David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and with a stone, and smote the Philistine, and slew him; but there was no sword in the hand of David.

Therefore David ran, and stood upon the Philistine, and took his sword, and drew it out of the sheath thereof, and slew him, and cut off his head therewith. And when the Philistines saw their champion was dead, they fled.

And the men of Israel and of Judah arose, and shouted, and pursued the Philistines, until thou come to the valley, and to the gates of Ekron. And the wounded of the Philistines fell down by the way to Shaaraim, even unto Gath, and unto Ekron.
And the children of Israel returned from chasing after the Philistines, and they spoiled their tents.
And David took the head of the Philistine, and brought it to Jerusalem; but he put his armour in his tent.
He played with lions as with kids, and with bears as with lambs.
Slew he not a giant, when he was yet but young? and did he not take away reproach from the people, when he lifted up his hand with the stone in the sling, and beat down the boasting of Goliath?
For he called upon the most high Lord; and he gave him strength in his right hand to slay that mighty warrior, and set up the horn of his people.
